newsitem.title: CANADA: Dayton sees mine producing 130,000 ozs.
newsitem.headline: Dayton sees mine producing 130,000 ozs.

text.p: Dayton Mining Corp said Friday it expects gold output at its Andocollo mine in Chile to reach 130,000 ounces this year from 88,000 ounces last year when a brief labor strike and technical problems cut production.
Dayton chief executive Wayne McClay told the company's annual meeting that harder than expected rock in the mine's main pit caused problems. Workers also went on strike for a week in December.
These caused 1996 production to fall below the 100,000 ounces Dayton had projected.
But the problems have now been resolved and a new contract settled, he said.
Gold production at the mine was on target at 23,500 ounces in the first quarter and is forecast to hit 160,000 ounces by 1999, he said.
Exploration boosted the resource estimate for the property by 700,000 ounces to three million last year and Dayton is planning to expand its capacity at the Andacollo plant.
Dayton is also "aggressively pursuing the acquisition of quality gold assets worldwide," McClay said. South and North America and Australia are its main areas of interest.
